newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL palm oil ends up on supportive factors.
newsitem.headline: KL palm oil ends up on supportive factors.

text.p: PALM OIL FUTURES PALM OIL PHYSICAL
May (3rd pos) 1,276 rgt/tonne Mar (south) 1,320*
Open/Hi/Low 1,268/1,278/1,264 Prev close 1,315
Prev settlement 1,264 * sellers prices

PALM OIL FUTURES - Prices ended firmer on rumour that Pakistan cut its import duty and news that India did not raise import duty to 30 percent. Expectation of slower palm oil output growth in Malaysia also supported sentiment. Buying emerged when May futures reached 1,270. Next resistance is seen at 1,300.
PALM OIL PHYSICAL - Some business was seen among products and nearby crude palm oil with hedging activity also evident.
Malaysia's palm oil output is expected to reach 8.9 million tonnes this year, up 6.1 percent over 1996.
Sentiment also improved after India did not announce a raise in import duty tariffs on edible oil in its 1997/1998 budget.
Earlier, there were rumours that India may raise its import duty to 30 percent from 20 pct, pushing Malaysian palm oil prices lower.
"The market was firm this morning particularly because of the Pakistan rumours but trading was slow," a trader said.
"The Pakistan rumour has a bullish impact on the market. If the cut is true, then we may see Pakistan buying more oils."
A Pakistani dealer said at the weekend the government planned to cut import duty by 1,000 rupees per tonne.
"The market has already reacted to the Pakistan rumour this morning," a trader with a commission house in Kuala Lumpur said.
"If the cut is confirmed, we will see vegetable oils, including palm oil, gain further ground. A cut will mean that it is much cheaper for Pakistan to buy oil," the trader added.
Turnover on the futures market was 1,458 lots at the close.
At the close, third month May futures contract ended 12 ringgit higher at 1,276 ringgit ($513.27) a tonne after trading between 1,264 and 1,278 ringgit.

Among physicals, Mar (south) crude palm oil was offered at 1,320 ringgit against bids of 1,315 after trading at 1312.50 and 1,315. Mar (central) saw offers at 1,310 against bids of 1,305 with earlier trades done at 1,305 and 1,302.50.
Apr (south) was offered at 1,310 with bids at 1,305 with early transactions at 1,300 and 1,305, and Apr (central) offered at 1,305 with bids at 1,295.
Among refined products, Mar RBD palm oil was offered at $560 a tonne FOB Malaysia, and Apr at $555. Mar was traded at $558.
Mar RBD palm olein saw offers at $592.50, Apr at $585 and May/Jun at $577.50. Apr was dealt at $585, $588 and $590.
Mar RBD palm stearin was offered at $462.50 and Mar/Apr palm fatty acid distillate saw sellers at $312.50.
